title: LLAMA LIMA: A Living Meta-Analysis on the Effects of Generative AI on Learning Mathematics (Version 2, 03/26)
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether generative AI–based instructional interventions improve mathematics learning and which factors shape their effectiveness. It is framed as a living meta-analysis because the field is changing quickly and conventional reviews may become outdated before publication.

The authors synthesize experimental and quasi-experimental studies of generative AI in mathematics education, including studies using ChatGPT-like systems, AI tutors, chatbots, and related tools. The review includes peer-reviewed journal articles, conference proceedings, edited book chapters, and eligible preprints. Across the coded studies, generative AI was used for multiple purposes such as assessment and feedback, direct instruction, mathematics problem solving, and teacher support.

The meta-analysis includes 21 studies and 38 effect sizes from 4,071 participants across several educational levels, including elementary, lower secondary, upper secondary, bachelor’s-level learners, adults, and some unspecified K-12 samples. Most studies were short, context-specific interventions, often using AI as a supplement to instruction. The pooled effect was positive but modest (g = 0.42), with wide credible intervals and substantial heterogeneity, suggesting that generative AI may support mathematics learning but effects vary considerably by context and implementation. The authors conclude that the evidence base is still limited and that stronger studies and future moderator analyses are needed.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a living meta-analysis following PRISMA-LSR guidelines with Bayesian multilevel meta-analysis, explicit effect-size extraction, sensitivity analyses, and publication-bias checks. Although the evidence base is still limited and heterogeneous, the methodology is strong and directly synthesizes experimental and quasi-experimental studies.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effect on mathematics learning is medium in size (g=0.42), exceeding the blue-tier threshold of 0.20. The estimate is promising for school mathematics, including adjacent evidence relevant to middle school implementation, though uncertainty remains due to heterogeneity and a still-small evidence base.

interventions.use_case: living meta-analysis of generative AI and large language model interventions for mathematics learning, including ChatGPT-style tutoring, chatbot help, AI-generated explanations, and adaptive feedback in school and university mathematics

finding.finding_summary: This living meta-analysis synthesized 21 studies and 38 effect sizes from 4,071 participants, estimating an overall positive effect of generative AI–based interventions on mathematics learning of g=0.42. The 95% credible interval was wide [0.13, 0.72], indicating uncertainty and substantial heterogeneity across studies, but the average effect is positive on mathematics achievement/performance outcomes.
finding.measure: mathematics learning outcomes / mathematics performance (varied study-specific achievement measures)
